 Dated this the 19th day of January, 2026  JUDGMENT

This writ petition is filed seeking the following reliefs:
"i. Issue a Writ of Mandamus or any appropriate writ order or direction commanding the respondents 1 to 3 to ensure that the 4th respondent does not run a hotel in building no. 6/646 belonging to the petitioner without a license issued by the respondents 1 and 2.

ii. Issue a Writ of Mandamus or any appropriate writ order or direction commanding the 3rd respondent to render necessary assistance to the respondents 1 and 2 to ensure that the 4th respondent does not run Olive Hotel without a license.
iii. Issue a Writ of Mandamus or any appropriate writ order or direction commanding the 3rd respondent to conduct a detailed enquiry on Ext P11 representation submitted by the petitioner and take follow up action.
iv. Grant such other relief deemed fit to this Hon'ble court."

sentences.text:
2 2. When this writ petition came up for consideration on 01.12.2025, this Court passed the following order:
"Admit.
Advocate K.B.Gangesh takes notice for respondents 1 and 2.
Learned Government Pleader takes notice for the 3rd respondent.
Issue notice to respondents 4 and 5 through speed post.

In the meanwhile, if the hotel of respondents 4 and 5 is functioning without the requisite license, the Panchayat shall take emergent measures to close down the hotel."
3.
Thereafter an application was filed by respondents 2026:KER:4206 4 and 5 to vacate the above order by filing I.A No.1/2026.
That application was dismissed by this Court on 13.01.2026.

The order passed in I.A No.1/2026 is extracted hereunder:
"Read order dated 01.12.2025.
I see no reason to vacate the order dated 01.12.2025.
The counsel appearing for the applicant in this Interlocutory application submitted that, he has got deemed license.
The same is objected by the Writ Petitioner.
I do not want to make any observation.

This court only observed that the hotel of respondent Nos.4 and 5 in the Writ Petition can function only with requisite license and if there is no requisite license, the Panchayat has to take emergency measures.
There is nothing to modify the above order at this stage.

Accordingly, the above application is dismissed. "
4.
Now, this Court as per judgment dated 19.01.2026 in WP(C.) No.1648/2026, allowed the party respondents to file a renewal application.
Therefore, this writ petition need not be retained, and the interim order passed by this Court can be continued.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that, there may be a direction to consider Ext.P11 by the 3rd respondent.
The 3rd respondent is the Station House Officer, Peramanagalam Police Station.
According to the petitioner, Ext.P11 make out cognizable offences.

If the police authorities are not taking any action in a complaint filed 2026:KER:4206 by the petitioner, there are remedies in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS'), either to approach the senior of the Police Officer or to approach the jurisdictional Magistrate Court with appropriate complaints.
This writ petition is disposed of retaining the interim order dated 01.12.2025, and also with a liberty to the petitioner to do the needful in accordance with the provisions of the BNSS.
